text: I've noticed that I stay a lot calmer when things go wrong at work. Before the experience a deadline or an angry client could ruin my whole week, I'd lie awake replaying conversations. Now I can feel the stress coming up and I take a few deep breaths, almost like during the trip when I focused on my breathing to get through the intense part. It doesn't always work but most of the time I can stay with the situation instead of spiralling.
Keine Veränderung feststellbar
I realise now that most of the stressful things are temporary. Whatever happens, it will pass, and in a year I probably won't even remember it. That makes it easier to not get overwhelmed.

The experience showed me where a lot of my stress reactions come from. When someone raises their voice I freeze, and during the trip I went back to being 7 years old and hiding under the table while my parents fought. I saw that the freeze is that little kid trying to protect himself. Since then, when I get into a stressful situation, especially conflicts, I can sometimes recognise that it's the old reaction and not the actual situation. I tell myself, you're not 7 anymore, you can speak. It doesn't make the stress go away but I understand it, and I'm less ashamed of it. I also told my partner about this so she understands why I go quiet.
Ich kann belastende Situationen besser annehmen und muss nicht mehr sofort dagegen ankämpfen. Das spart viel Kraft.

Honestly it made it worse. The experience was a bad trip and for months afterwards any stress at all would trigger a feeling of panic and unreality, like I was back in it. I avoided crowded places and stressful conversations. It's better now, two years later, but I'm still more sensitive to stress than I was before.
Better at staying calm

Ich habe durch die Erfahrung gelernt, dass schwierige Situationen zum Leben dazugehören und dass ich sie nicht vermeiden muss. Früher habe ich mich bei Problemen sofort zurückgezogen, habe mich krankgemeldet oder bin Konflikten aus dem Weg gegangen. Während der Erfahrung musste ich durch eine sehr schwierige Phase hindurch, in der ich große Angst hatte, und habe gemerkt, dass es auf der anderen Seite besser wird, wenn ich nicht weglaufe. Das versuche ich seitdem im Alltag umzusetzen. Als letztes Jahr mein Vater schwer krank wurde, war ich für ihn da und habe mich der Situation gestellt, statt in Panik zu geraten. Ich habe auch gelernt, mit meiner Familie offener über Sorgen zu sprechen, und wir haben uns gegenseitig sehr unterstützt. Ich sehe belastende Ereignisse jetzt eher als Teil eines größeren Ganzen, die mich wachsen lassen.

After the experience I started meditating every morning for 10-15 minutes. When something stressful happens I use the breathing technique from my practice, and I go for a run if I can. These habits help me deal with stress much better than before.
Not sure. I haven't had any major stressful events since then, so hard to say if anything changed.
Ich bin in Stresssituationen deutlich gelassener als früher, auch im Job.

I'm much more willing to talk to people when I'm struggling. I used to bottle things up and deal with them alone. Now I call a friend or my sister, and I've even talked to my manager about my workload. It makes a huge difference.

The experience gave me a completely different perspective on what matters. During the trip I had this overwhelming sense of how small and short my life is, in the scale of the universe, and at the same time how precious every moment is. When I came back to normal life, a lot of the things that used to stress me out just seemed so trivial. A rude comment from a colleague, a traffic jam, a bad grade. I still notice the stress but it doesn't have the same grip on me. It's like I can zoom out and see that this is just one small moment in a long life, and that I will be fine. Even bigger things, like when my relationship ended last year, I was very sad, but I didn't feel like my world was ending. I knew that this too will pass, and that there is a bigger picture. I think this is the most lasting change from the experience, more than any specific insight, a sort of background trust that things work out somehow even if I don't see how yet. My friends have noticed that I am the calm one now in a crisis.

Mir ist durch die Erfahrung bewusst geworden, dass ich in Stresssituationen sehr schnell in alte Muster verfalle, vor allem in Selbstvorwürfe. Ich erkenne das jetzt früher und kann manchmal gegensteuern, indem ich mir sage, dass ich nicht an allem schuld bin. Das gelingt nicht immer, aber ich verstehe besser, was in mir passiert, wenn ich unter Druck gerate.
I don't freak out as much when stuff goes wrong

I've learned to accept the things I can't change, and focus on what I can do. When my mother was diagnosed with dementia, I would have been completely lost before. This time I let myself be sad, but I also saw that this is how life goes, people get old, and that I can choose how I spend the time we have left. I visit her every week and I enjoy those visits, even when she doesn't recognise me.
Seit der Erfahrung gab es keine größeren Belastungen, daher kann ich das nicht beurteilen.
I'm calmer in general and I don't get stressed so easily, especially in traffic and at home with the kids.

Before the experience I would always react to stress with anger. I would yell at my partner, slam doors, sometimes punch walls. I hated myself for it afterwards. During the experience I saw my anger very clearly, as a kind of shield. Underneath it was fear, fear of not being good enough, of being abandoned. Seeing this has changed how I handle stressful situations. When I feel the anger coming up now, I try to stop and ask myself what I'm afraid of. Often I can then talk about the fear instead of exploding. I've also started therapy to work on this, and I use some techniques from there, like counting to ten and leaving the room for a few minutes. My partner says I'm much easier to live with. I still mess up sometimes but it's maybe 20% of what it used to be.
Ich sehe Probleme jetzt eher aus einer gewissen Distanz. Vieles, was mich früher stark belastet hat, erscheint mir heute weniger wichtig. Ich weiß, dass das Leben weitergeht.

I don't think it changed much in how I handle stress, maybe a bit worse at the start because I felt unsettled for a while after the experience. Now I'm back to how I was before. Stress is stress, I deal with it the same way, mostly by working through it and then crashing on the weekend.
Less reactive. I take a moment before responding to stressful emails now.

Ich habe gelernt, belastende Gefühle zuzulassen, statt sie wegzudrücken. In der Erfahrung kam sehr viel Trauer hoch, über den Tod meiner Schwester vor einigen Jahren, und ich habe das erste Mal richtig geweint. Seitdem gehe ich anders mit schwierigen Situationen um. Wenn ich traurig oder ängstlich bin, lasse ich das zu und weiß, dass es vorbeigeht. Als ich letzten Winter meinen Job verloren habe, konnte ich die Enttäuschung fühlen, ohne mich davon überrollen zu lassen.

I'm better at asking for help. When my business was struggling last year, I reached out to old friends and a mentor instead of trying to fix everything myself, which I would have done before. I think the experience made me feel more connected to people and less like I have to prove I can do it all alone.
I don't panic as fast as I used to when something unexpected happens

Ich bin ruhiger geworden und rege mich über viele Dinge nicht mehr so auf. Wenn etwas schiefgeht, denke ich mir oft, dass es Schlimmeres gibt, und dass ich das schon irgendwie hinkriege. Das hat mir vor allem in meiner Prüfungsphase geholfen.

I've developed a few practices that help me with stress since the experience: I journal in the evenings, I go for walks without my phone, and I do a short body scan when I notice I'm tense. I didn't do any of that before. I think the experience showed me that my body holds a lot of stress and that I need to take care of it actively.

This is a difficult question because I think the experience changed many things at once. The most important thing for handling stress is that I understand myself a lot better. I grew up in a household with a lot of chaos, my dad drank and my mom was depressed, and I learned very early to be hypervigilant, to read the room, to take care of everyone. When I'm under stress, I go into that mode automatically: I try to control everything, I don't sleep, I work all the time and I don't ask for help. During the experience, I saw this pattern so clearly, like a film of my life, and I saw how much it has cost me. I also saw that I don't need to do this anymore, that I'm safe now. Since then I notice when I'm going into control mode and I try to stop, take a breath and ask myself what I actually need. Sometimes it's just rest. I've also started to set more boundaries with my family, which has reduced a lot of my stress. It's an ongoing process but I'm much better at it than before.
Bin gelassener, wenn es stressig wird
I see stressful events more as challenges than threats now. I remember that during the experience I went through something very scary and came out okay, so I trust that I can do that again.
I can handle stress at work much better, I stay calm in meetings and I don't take criticism so personally anymore.

Ich nehme belastende Ereignisse inzwischen eher an, als mich dagegen zu wehren. Früher habe ich mich tagelang über Dinge geärgert, die ich nicht ändern konnte, z.B. über Entscheidungen meines Chefs oder über das Verhalten meiner Schwiegermutter. Heute sage ich mir: Das ist jetzt so, was kann ich daraus machen? Das hilft mir sehr, und ich bin weniger erschöpft.

I'm better at handling stressful events because I feel more connected to the people around me. When my dad passed away last year, I let my friends support me, I talked about it, I cried with my partner. In the past I would have shut down. I also try to be there for others more, and I think that sense of being part of a community makes everything feel less heavy. I'm generally calmer, I sleep better even when things are hard, and I don't get as overwhelmed as I used to.
Hard to say, nothing really

Durch die Erfahrung habe ich verstanden, warum ich in belastenden Situationen immer so stark mit Rückzug reagiere. Ich habe in der Erfahrung Szenen aus meiner Kindheit gesehen, in denen ich mich allein in meinem Zimmer verkrochen habe, weil zu Hause niemand für mich da war. Ich habe damals gelernt, alles allein auszuhalten. Heute merke ich, wenn ich wieder in diesen Rückzug gehe, und versuche bewusst, mich an andere zu wenden. Ich habe auch gelernt, meine Gefühle in solchen Momenten anzunehmen und nicht gleich zu bewerten. Ich bin nicht mehr so streng mit mir, wenn ich in einer Krise nicht perfekt funktioniere. Das hat mir zum Beispiel geholfen, als ich mich im letzten Jahr von meinem Partner getrennt habe.
Stressful things just seem smaller now. I look at the bigger picture and I don't get so caught up in the drama of the moment.
I'm more relaxed in general and less likely to get stressed about small things
Ich mache seit der Erfahrung regelmäßig Yoga und Atemübungen. Wenn ich gestresst bin, gehe ich in den Wald oder höre Musik. Das hilft mir sehr, wieder runterzukommen.

I think I've become more accepting of the ups and downs of life. Stressful events still happen, but I don't see them as a personal attack from the universe anymore. During the experience I felt that everything is connected and that there is a flow to life. When something bad happens now, I try to go with it rather than against it. I still have stress, of course, but I recover much faster.
A little calmer maybe. Not a big change though.
